title: Instructions
body:
* The indirect result of an instruction are the [[Status Bits]]
* Numbers (#) can be prefixed by $(hex), @(octal), %(binary), no prefix means decimal. 

# Basic Instructions

### Data Movement
`move.<x>     <# or address>,<address>`
`clr.<x>      <dest>`
* Same as moving 0 to destination.
### Addition / Subtraction
`add.<x>     <src>,<dest> 
* either the source or the destination must be a data register. 
`adda.<x>    <src>,<dest>`
* "add address"
* cannot give data registers, only address registers.

`sub.<x>      <src>,<dest>`
use either:
* (1) destination - source 
* (2) destination + NEG(source) (2's comp)
If using (2) 

### Extensions
`ext.<x>      <dest>`
* Extends whatever is in destination to size x.

The rest of the instruction set, which this note does not cover:
[[Branching and Looping]] (`bra`, `bcc`, `dbra`), [[Subroutines]] (`jsr`, `rts`, the stack),
[[Binary Operations]] (`and`, `or`, `eor`, shifts), and [[Mathematical Operations]]
(`muls`, `divu`). Operands are written in one of four [[Addressing Modes]].
